title: The Broken Rivergate
premise: Dominic Brightwater has spent a decade outrunning her mother's famous name and the dig that killed her father, drifting between salvage crews and border towns. When the prospector Ede Voss trades her a hand-drawn map of the Broken Rivergate for a promise to finish what he started, Dominic finds the site where her parents' last expedition vanished—and evidence that her mother didn't die in an accident but sealed something away on purpose. Pursued by the Meridian Institute, which funded the original dig and wants its secrets, Dominic must lead a small crew through the flooded canyon, decide whether to expose or protect what the Rivergate holds, and finally choose between the inheritance she's been fleeing and the people she's learned to love. In the end she collapses the gate behind them, publishes only enough truth to clear her mother's name, and stays—rooted for the first time—in the town where it all began.
about_author: X. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former field surveyor who spent six seasons mapping river systems across three continents before turning to fiction. Sterling writes adventure novels about people who are better at leaving than staying.

chapters.title: The Weight of Staying
chapters.summary: Dominic Brightwater, working a salvage crew in the border town of Callow's Bend, plans to slip out before anyone learns her surname. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: restless self-containment; she's already halfway gone when the story starts.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Dying prospector Ede Voss corners Dominic in a boarding house, recognizing her by her digging hands. He trades a map of the Broken Rivergate for her promise to finish his work. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: unease curdling into obligation—a debt she can't refuse.

chapters.title: What the Name Costs
chapters.summary: Word spreads that a Brightwater is in town; a Meridian Institute surveyor named Halvard arrives asking questions. Dominic realizes her anonymity is already spent. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: the old dread of being seen, sharpened by Halvard's polite menace.

chapters.title: The Crew She Swore She Wouldn't Gather
chapters.summary: Dominic recruits three locals: ferryman Ilsa Rook, demolitions man Tam Ovid, and archivist Juno Pell—who once idolized her mother. POV: Dominic with a Juno interlude. Emotional beat: reluctant trust forming against her will.

chapters.title: Downriver at First Light
chapters.summary: The expedition launches. Halvard follows openly now, claiming Institute jurisdiction over the Rivergate concession. First night camp, Juno confronts Dominic about her mother's final letters. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: friction hardening into fragile alliance.

chapters.title: The Drowned Canyon
chapters.summary: They enter the gorge where the river runs beneath stone. Ede's map proves eerily accurate—including markings in her mother's handwriting that predate Ede's copy. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: awe tangled with grief; the past is physically underfoot.

chapters.title: Ede's Last Camp
chapters.summary: They find Ede's abandoned camp and his journal: he saw what the first expedition found, and it broke him. The journal hints her mother sealed something 'for everyone's good.' POV: Juno reading aloud. Emotional beat: dread replacing curiosity.

chapters.title: Halvard's Offer
chapters.summary: Halvard catches up, offering funding, protection, and erasure of Dominic's debts if she surrenders the map. She refuses; he warns the river rises in nine days. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: defiance laced with doubt about who the villain really is.

chapters.title: The First Gate
chapters.summary: The crew breaches the outer gate—an ancient flood-control works, not a tomb. Inside: tools from her parents' expedition, arranged deliberately, like a message. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: wonder undercut by the sense of being expected.

chapters.title: Letters in Stone
chapters.summary: Deciphering her mother's markers, Dominic learns the expedition found a living aquifer system the Institute meant to strip-mine—and her mother flooded the lower chambers to stop them, dying in the process. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: the inheritance revealed as sacrifice, not shame.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Crossing
chapters.summary: A flash flood traps Ilsa; Dominic's rescue nearly kills them both and costs half their supplies. Trust deepens into something unspoken between them. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: love surfacing where duty said keep moving.

chapters.title: The Turncoat
chapters.summary: Juno, desperate for her mother's legacy to be celebrated rather than buried, secretly signals Halvard's position. Dominic discovers the betrayal but says nothing yet. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: guilt and rationalization warring.

chapters.title: The Second Gate
chapters.summary: They reach the inner chamber: the aquifer heart, still alive, still holding. Evidence shows the Institute knew all along and let the first expedition die covering its tracks. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the enemy was never abstract.

chapters.title: Nine Days Become Three
chapters.summary: Seasonal melt accelerates; Halvard's team begins blasting the upper canyon to force entry. The crew must move now or lose everything. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: ticking-clock panic compressing every choice.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Weir
chapters.summary: Dominic confronts Halvard directly, offering him the truth in exchange for withdrawal; he refuses—exposure would end the Institute. Juno's signal is revealed. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: betrayal met not with rage but with terrible understanding.

chapters.title: What Juno Carried
chapters.summary: Juno confesses: she wanted her hero back, whole and public. Dominic gives her the real choice—help seal the gate or walk out and live with it. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Rising
chapters.summary: Halvard's blast cracks the upper weir early. Water begins reclaiming the canyon as the crew races to place charges that will collapse the inner gate permanently. POV: alternating, rapid cuts. Emotional beat: terror fused with purpose.

chapters.title: Her Mother's Hands
chapters.summary: In the flooding chamber, Dominic performs the same manual override her mother used—understanding, finally, why she stayed. Ilsa pulls her out at the last second. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: climax of identity; she stops running by choosing to stay and act.

chapters.title: The Gate Falls
chapters.summary: The inner gate collapses; the aquifer seals itself. Halvard's team retreats as the canyon floods behind them. The crew escapes soaked, diminished, alive. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: exhausted, hard-won relief.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Back in Callow's Bend, Dominic drafts a public account clearing her mother's name—naming the Institute's cover-up but omitting the aquifer's location. Halvard's superiors bury the scandal quietly. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: justice partial but real; memory honored without being sold.

chapters.title: Roots
chapters.summary: Ede's promise fulfilled, Dominic faces the open road one last time—and unpacks instead. She and Ilsa take over the ferry crossing; Juno archives the true story under seal. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: quiet joy; staying chosen, not surrendered.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Its Own
chapters.summary: A year later, spring melt swells the river harmlessly past the new crossing. A stranger arrives asking about the Rivergate; Dominic smiles and points downstream. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: peace earned; some inheritances are kept by silence, and she keeps hers well.
